question: How did researchers in Idaho in 2017 finally show that seeding clouds had made snow fall?
answer: By making the snow carry a signature. An aircraft laid silver iodide across winter clouds in lines back and forth across the wind, and radar then showed matching lines of snow drifting downwind, a pattern no natural storm draws. Seven decades of seeding trials had failed to separate seeded snow from ordinary snow.
move: When no control is possible, make the effect sign its own name.
ask: When I cannot run a control, how could I make an effect prove it came from me?
reference: French et al., Precipitation formation from orographic cloud seeding, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2018
